main_body: Two timber-framed gabled houses joined by a lower connecting wall, with steep tiled roofs above plaster and timber front walls
top_band: Large terracotta roof slope in light orange and cream highlights over mid and dark tile rows, from about row 20 to row 75 in the centre column; the column scan shows repeating tile highlight and shadow stripes
evidence: The roof is a big, clearly lit tiled surface seen from above, with side slopes and hips visible. Below it the plaster and half-timber front face has its own shading. A dark eave line and shadow separate the two at the gable base, and the windows have sills and dark inset frames. The construction matches the reference house-h101_0, where the roof slope reads as the top surface above a vertical wall.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have per-tile highlights, mid, dark and deep tones. The plaster has speckle, the timbers have grain and beam shading, and the window boxes carry small coloured dots. Outlines are dark brown or dark red-brown rather than neutral black; only 5% of dark edge pixels are neutral. There are 195 distinct colours, 11 per tile (references: 18 and 11), and 0% flat-fill coverage. This sits at or above the stone reference and just below h101_0 on density, so it would not look thinner next to either.
